edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a protective direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.mechanism: Amplification reduces auditory deprivation and the cognitive load of decoding speech, which may preserve social engagement and slow downstream cognitive decline.
edges.summary: What makes this pair believable is not one flashy paper but the way the literature stacks up: the 2024 Okano cohort in Psychogeriatrics already points to hearing aid use tracks with lower risk or better outcomes, and later studies mostly refine the size of the effect rather than overturning it. In practice this reads more like a real risk signal than a one-off finding.
edges.caveats: Healthier-user bias, screening intensity, and baseline risk can all inflate apparent benefit in observational work, so the magnitude should be read conservatively.
